title: Who carries the cards

item.name: The cards
item.line: 7 plain cream cards, each with an open eye drawn on it, found in 7 cases on Lantern Row.

brief: The letter that came to the art room had no name on it, and an open eye. That makes 7 cards in 7 cases, and the committee has had enough.
Every card was handed over in person, by somebody who knew each time what was about to happen on the street.
5 people were close to every case: Rosa, Marco, Otto, Bea and Mr Cole.
Before the committee cuts the ribbon on 2011, it wants to know whose hand it has been.

suspects.name: Rosa
suspects.line: Found a card in her own till. Says she has better things to do than hand them out.
suspects.says: I was at the coast with the night stall for half of those days.

suspects.name: Marco
suspects.line: Wanted 2011 read from the start. The street says that makes him the one.
suspects.says: I never leave my ovens before 9. Ask the bread.

suspects.name: Otto
suspects.line: Holds a key to the music cupboard, and the street has not forgotten it.
suspects.says: I open the hall for choir at 9, and never before.

suspects.name: Bea
suspects.line: Had the list of 20 names before anybody. The art room is next door to the hall.
suspects.says: I was sent the list. I never sent anything.

suspects.name: Mr Cole
suspects.line: 22 years of keys and the night round. Has never once talked about 2011.
suspects.says: I lock up and go home. I have said all I am going to say about 2011.

steps.thing: The committee's list of the 7 cards: where each was found, and on what day.
steps.fact: 7 cards in 6 weeks, each found within a day of its case. Rosa was at the coast with the night stall for 2 of those days, and the till rolls show it.
steps.lead: Whoever it is was on the street every time. Marco says he never leaves his ovens, and the bakery keeps a round sheet. It tore in 2 on the van door.

steps.thing: The bakery's round sheet for card days, torn top to bottom on the van door. Both halves were kept for the accounts.
page: Van out at 6 with the boy
Shop open at 9, Marco on till
steps.fact: On every day a card turned up, Marco was at his ovens from 4 until the shop opened at 9, with the van out and nobody else to mind the bread.
steps.lead: Not Marco. The cards in the hall were pinned up inside it. The watchman's log has the nights, with a gap in each.

steps.thing: The watchman's log for a card night, with a gap in it.

events: 10.30 pm. The night round: every door of the hall locked.
7 am. A card is found pinned up inside the locked hall.
9 am. Otto unlocks the hall for the choir.

options.text: Otto comes in early and pins it up.
It is pinned up from inside, by somebody who has the keys after the round.
It blows in under the door from the street.

steps.fact: Each card in the hall was pinned up inside, after the round locked the doors at 10.30 and before 7. After 10.30 only the round has keys. Otto never opened up before 9.
steps.lead: The street says the art room is next door to the hall, and that Bea works late.

steps.thing: The street's claim, set against the night round.

claim.says: Bea pinned them. The art room is next door, and she was there until 11 every card night.

facts.text: The cards turned up across 6 weeks.
After 10.30 the hall is locked, and only the round has keys.

steps.fact: It could not be done. Next door is not inside. After 10.30 the hall is locked, and Bea has never held a key to it.
steps.lead: Not Bea. This morning's card is still on the hall notice board, and it reads oddly.

steps.thing: This morning's card on the hall notice board. It carries a line in plain sight, to the Open Eye.
steps.text: Walk up Lane 4, past the rich old yew. Fair is fair.
steps.fact: Read the way the Open Eye teaches, it says: "Walk. Hold the plane. Fair." Whoever carries the cards held the plane in 2011, and wants the street to look again.
steps.lead: Walk the 7 cards back, from the first hooks to this morning's board, before anybody is named.

steps.thing: The case, walked once more through every place a card was left. Each find goes back where it was found.
steps.fact: Every card was left where the night round goes. And in the hall store the guillotine still has cream card in its tray, cut to the size of every card on the street.
steps.lead: A round with keys, the hall's own card, 6 weeks, and a plane held in 2011. They fit 1 of the 5.

steps.thing: The 5 from the brief, and what the evidence left standing.
steps.fact: Chance: inside the locked hall, after the round. Means: the keys of the round, and the hall's own card and guillotine. Motive: a plane held in 2011.

ending.found: 7 cards are gone from a stack of 40 in the hall store, cut on the hall guillotine. Mr Cole keeps the only key. The committee cuts the ribbon on 2011: the vote was 9 to 9, and the chair broke the tie.
ending.confession: I held the plane because the committee told me to. I waited 15 years for somebody to ask. I only made sure the street kept finding reasons to.
ending.after: R. MARLOW stays burned on the spoon. Asked who taught him the cards, Mr Cole will not say. He says only that he was asked once, by an open eye, and that he was glad to be.
